title: Finding Files
subtitle: find, locate, which, whereis — searching the filesystem by name and content
author: KERNAL Team

content.text: find — search by name, type, size, time

content.code:
# Find by name
find . -name "*.json"              # all .json files from current dir
find /var/log -name "*.log"        # all .log files in /var/log
find . -name "index.html" -type f  # only files, not dirs named index.html
find . -type d -name "node_modules"  # find node_modules directories

# Case-insensitive
find . -iname "readme*"            # matches README.md, readme.txt, Readme

# By size
find . -size +100M                 # files larger than 100MB
find . -size -1k                   # files smaller than 1KB

# By modification time
find . -mtime -7                   # modified in last 7 days
find . -mtime +30                  # not modified in 30 days

# Execute a command on each found file
find . -name "*.log" -exec rm {} \;        # delete all .log files
find . -name "*.sh" -exec chmod +x {} \;   # make all .sh executable
find . -name "*.png" -exec ls -lh {} \;    # show sizes of all PNGs

# Exclude directories
find . -name "*.js" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"

# Find where a command is installed
which python3       # /usr/bin/python3
which node          # /usr/local/bin/node
which git           # /usr/bin/git

# whereis: find binary, source, and man pages
whereis python3     # python3: /usr/bin/python3 /usr/lib/python3 ...

# type: shows what a command is (builtin, function, alias, or path)
type cd             # cd is a shell builtin
type ls             # ls is aliased to 'ls --color=auto'
type python3        # python3 is /usr/bin/python3

content.text: find is powerful but slow for large filesystems. locate uses a pre-built database and is much faster for searching by filename: locate '*.conf'. Update the database with: sudo updatedb. Use find for fresh results and complex criteria.

questions.question: You want to find all Python files in the current directory tree but skip the .venv/ folder. Which command works?
questions.explanation: find's -not -path pattern excludes paths matching the pattern. -path '*/.venv/*' matches any path containing /.venv/, and -not inverts it. The pattern must use * wildcards that match across directories. find has no --exclude flag — use -not -path or -prune.

faq.q: How do I search for text inside files?
faq.a: Use grep, not find. find locates files by metadata (name, size, date). grep searches file contents: grep -r 'TODO' ./src/ searches all files in src/ for the text 'TODO'. Combine them: find . -name '*.js' | xargs grep 'console.log' to grep only JS files.

examples: find . -name '*.log' -mtime +7 -delete — delete log files older than 7 days, a common cron job on servers
find . -name 'node_modules' -type d -exec rm -rf {} + — remove all node_modules recursively from a monorepo
